author: pgaudet
body:
Hi @LiNiMGI 

The Extracellular Matrix experts from Matrisome tell us that THSD4 (MGI:2672033) is not in the microfibril. Can you please check the annotation? And ask any question here. 

Thanks, Pascale

author: LiNiMGI
body:
@pgaudet MGI Microfibril (GO:0001527) annotation for THSD4 was from PMID: 19940141. The paper shows THSD4 is not itself a core structural microfibril protein like fibrillin, it is considered a microfibril-associated protein that regulates microfibril formation and stability. So does that mean THSD4 "is active in" microfibril?
@DaiqingChen If MGI removes the Microfibril (GO:0001527) annotation for THSD4, do you have a preferred replacement? Or just annotate to the broader Extracellular matrix (GO:0031012)? Thanks, Li

author: pgaudet
body:
Hi @LiNiMGI 

> THSD4 (...) is considered a microfibril-associated protein that regulates microfibril formation and stability. So does that mean THSD4 "is active in" microfibril?


No.- if it's not part of the complex, it cannot be active in the complex. In this case the complex may be its input (possibly, but I didn't check if the evidence supports that). Do you agree?

author: pgaudet
body:
@DaiqingChen 

Li and I are looking at this one together. There are two points we'd like to clarify: 
1. Can you suggest another cellular location for THSD4 ? 
2. The definition for 'microfibril' is "Extracellular matrix components occurring independently or along with elastin. Thought to have force-bearing functions in tendon. In addition to fibrillins, **microfibrils may contain other associated proteins**." >> that last part of the definition should be fixed to something less vague. But can we more specific about what proteins are composing the microfibril ? that would really help. 
Thanks, Pascale

author: DaiqingChen
body:
> [@DaiqingChen](https://github.com/DaiqingChen)
> 
> Li and I are looking at this one together. There are two points we'd like to clarify:
> 
> 1. Can you suggest another cellular location for THSD4 ?
> 2. The definition for 'microfibril' is "Extracellular matrix components occurring independently or along with elastin. Thought to have force-bearing functions in tendon. In addition to fibrillins, **microfibrils may contain other associated proteins**." >> that last part of the definition should be fixed to something less vague. But can we more specific about what proteins are composing the microfibril ? that would really help.
>    Thanks, Pascale

Hi Pascale,
1. I'm suggesting to put THSD4 (ADAMSTL6) in Elastic fiber, see #6253 . The reference we use PMID: 23962539 says THSD4 "Probably associated with microfibrils", to us it's not a definite yes of being located/active in microfibril. Elastic fiber is the direct parent of microfibrils, hence we suggest to put any potential protein that is unsure about their exact location in Elastic fiber.
2. I agree that the last sentence is pretty vague. Maybe we can change the last sentence to "The major component of microfibril is fibrillins and Microfibrillar-associated proteins (MFAPs)." What do you think?

Thank you!

author: pgaudet
body:
Thanks @DaiqingChen 

Can we be more specific? According to Google AI overview : 

> Microfibrillar-Associated Proteins (MFAPs)
Subfamily Members: The family includes MFAP1, MFAP2 (also known as MAGP-1), MFAP3, MFAP4, and MFAP5 (also known as MAGP-2).


Is this correct ? 

Thanks, Pascale

author: LiNiMGI
DaiqingChen
body:
> [@DaiqingChen](https://github.com/DaiqingChen) Thank you for your feedback regarding the THSD4 (ADAMTSL6) annotation. While the reference you mentioned (PMID: 23962539) uses the phrase "probably associated with microfibrils," several other reports (PMID:19940141 PMID:21880733. PMID:32855533. PMID:32141660) including more recent findings—consistently demonstrate that THSD4 is a specific protein localized within the microfibril and actively involved in microfibril dynamics... Given that some of the later studies provide a more definitive and contemporary view than the 2013 reference, should MGI keep the THSD4 (ADAMTSL6) microfibril annotation? Thanks! Li

Hi Li,
That make sense, if there's enough evidence showing that THSD4 is indeed active in microfibril, let's keep it in the microfibril. Thank you!

Best,
Daiqing
